figures.caption: FIGURE 1 Structural and morphological characterization of Li10 + 2x SnP2 − x Inx S12 (x = 0, 0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2). (a) Schematic illustration of the synthesis process. (b) XRD patterns of Li10 + 2x SnP2 − x Inx S12 . (c) Enlarged XRD patterns of the Li10 + 2x SnP2 − x Inx S12 SSEs in the 2 𝜃range from 14◦to 35◦. (d) Raman spectra of Li10 + 2x SnP2 − x Inx S12 . (e) XRD patterns and corresponding Rietveld refinements of Li10.2 SnP1.9 In0.1 S12 (LSPS-In). (f) S 2p XPS spectra of LSPS-In and LSPS. (g) Formation energies of In substitution at the Wyckoff 4d and 2a sites. (h) TEM image and corresponding EDS mappings of LSPS-In. (i) HRTEM image of region 1 marked in Figure 1h for LSPS-In.

FIGURE 2 Li+ conduction properties of Li10 + 2x SnP2 − x Inx S12 . (a) Nyquist plots and (b) ionic conductivities at 25◦C. (c) Direct-current polarization curves. (d) Nyquist plots and (e) ionic conductivities at − 15◦C. (f) Nyquist plots of LSPS-In at different temperatures (25◦C-90◦C). (g) Arrhenius plots of the temperature-dependent ionic conductivities. (h) Ionic conductivity of LSPS and LSPS-In before and after air exposure. (i) CV curves of LSPS and LSPS-In in the voltage range of − 0.5 to 5 V.

FIGURE 3 Electrochemical behavior and post-cycling interfacial characterization of Li symmetric cells. CCD tests of (a) Li/LSPS/Li and (b) Li/LSPS-In/Li cells. (c) Long-term Li plating/stripping performance at 0.1 mA cm− 2 and 25◦C, with enlarged voltage profiles shown in the insets. Depth- resolved S 2p, P 2p, and Sn 3d XPS spectra of the electrolyte-contacting Li metal surfaces recovered from (d–f) Li/LSPS-In/Li and (g–i) Li/LSPS/Li cells after 100 h of cycling at 0.1 mA cm− 2 , collected at sputtering depths of 0, 60, 150, and 300 nm.

FIGURE 4 Li+ migration barriers, electronic structures, and solid-state NMR analyses of LSPS-In and LSPS. (a) Representative Li+ migration trajectories between two Li1 sites at the 16 h Wyckoff position, evaluated using the CI-NEB method for LSPS and LSPS-In, and (b) corresponding migration energy profiles. Band structures and DOS of (c) LSPS-In and (f) LSPS. Differential charge density maps of (d) LSPS-In and (g) LSPS. (e) 31 P and (h) 7 Li solid-state NMR spectra of LSPS-In and LSPS.

FIGURE 5 Electrochemical performance of ASSBs and Li metal batteries at 25◦C. (a) Rate performance of NCM83@B2 O3 /Li-In batteries. (b) Cycling performance of NCM83@B2 O3 /Li-In batteries at 1 C. (c) Long term cycling performance of NCM83@B2 O3 /LSPS-In/Li-In battery at 5 C. (d) Comparison of initial capacity, cycling performance, and capacity retention with reported Ni-rich cathode/sulfide electrolyte ASSBs. (e) Rate performance of NCM83@B2 O3 /Li batteries. (f) Cycling stability of NCM83@B2 O3 /Li batteries at 0.5 C.

figures.label: S24
figures.caption: Figure S24 Electrochemical performance of NCM83@B2O3/Li-In batteries at 1 C and 55°C. (a) Cycling performance of batteries using LSPS-In and LSPS electrolytes. Charge/discharge profiles of (b) the LSPS-In-based and (c) the LSPS-based batteries. Corresponding dQ/dV curves of (d) the LSPS-In-based and (e) the LSPS-based batteries. The charge-discharge profiles of the LSPS-In-based battery remain highly overlapped from the 1st to the 400th cycle with limited polarization growth while the LSPS-based battery shows pronounced polarization increase and capacity fading. Consistently, dQ/dV analysis shows well-defined redox peaks with a small peak shift of 0.012 V for the LSPS-In-based battery after 400 cycles, in contrast to severe peak broadening and a larger peak shift of 0.106 V for the LSPS-based battery.
